passage: On a sunny afternoon, four toddlers were trying to get onto the sofa. Aparna lay on her tummy across the cushion, then hooked a knee up, then rolled sideways, and stayed with the way that got her knee over the edge. Pallavi had watched her older brother turn round, sit and swing his legs up. She copied the order of it loosely and ended up half on the seat, nearer than she had ever got. Kamal scrambled up the high arm of the sofa rather than the seat. He slipped, and his grandmother, standing beside him, caught him before he hit the floor. Little Divya had once got a knee onto the edge of the cushion, and it had helped. Now she began each climb that way, and she got quicker every day.

qa.q: Who caught Kamal when he slipped?
How does Kamal's climb differ from Aparna's, and what happened to each?
qa.a: Kamal scrambled at the tall armrest and slipped, needing to be caught, while Aparna tried several ways and stayed with the one that worked.

qa.q: What might Kamal be feeling right after he slips?
qa.a: He is probably startled and maybe a little scared, since he was so eager that he did not check the spot.

qa.q: How could a caregiver help Kamal climb more safely?
qa.a: A caregiver could stay close, guide him to the seat rather than the armrest, and show the knee-first way that worked for others. 🙂

grounding: Four toddlers climb onto a sofa by trial and error, copying an older sibling, scrambling impulsively, and repeating a move that worked.
